extracted.intended_audience: NIH study-section reviewers, NIH program officers, and SBIR/STTR grant program staff (and other grant reviewers assessing preclinical IND-enabling proposals)
extracted.subtask_description: A preclinical grant application describing peptide therapeutics to prevent/reverse type 1 diabetes in NOD mice with the aim of identifying a lead candidate and generating IND-enabling data (PK, toxicology, immunogenicity). Contains Specific Aims, Significance, Innovation, Approach, Preliminary Data, Vertebrate Animal section and regulatory/IP notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific Aims
rubrics_metrics.description: Goals for Phase I: Establish a lead candidate peptide through (1) determining impact on glucose tolerance testing (GTT); (2) determining duration of protection KGYY15 versus KGYY6; (3) determining impact on insulin and c-peptide production. Goals for Phase II: determine impacted cell types, immunogenicity (short- and long-term), impact on natural immunity, extended pharmacokinetics, toxicity studies, with the end deliverable being an IND submission to the FDA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific aims must be clear, testable, and produce a lead candidate and IND-enabling endpoints. Phase I aims are mechanistic/efficacy readouts to support a Phase II that focuses on PK/toxicology/IND preparation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Establishes the public health importance (high prevalence and rising incidence of T1D), unmet medical need (no current therapies to prevent or restore insulin production), and that CD40-expressing T cells (Th40) are a pathogenic, translationally relevant biomarker/target (expanded in human T1D and pre-diabetic subjects).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A compelling application must quantify disease burden, show translational relevance of target (Th40 cells), and explain how controlling CD40 would change treatment paradigms. Evidence linking the biomarker to human disease strengthens significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: The approach is novel in using peptides derived from CD154 that encompass known receptor–ligand interaction hot spots to modulate CD40, avoiding complications of monoclonal antibodies and non-specific small organic molecules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Innovation is judged by methodological novelty (peptide vs antibodies/small molecules), specificity, and potential to avoid known antibody-related toxicities (e.g., anti-CD154 platelet aggregation). The application should emphasize how the method is 'entirely new' relative to prior approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach (overall experimental design)
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed preclinical experimental plans including GTT at multiple disease stages, dosing strategies (prevention: 1 mg/kg weekly; reversal: 4 mg/kg induction then maintenance), routes of administration (IV, IP, SC, IM), dose-escalation experiments, time courses up to 45 weeks, and concurrent measurement of functional and histologic endpoints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approach must include well-powered experimental groups, appropriate controls, clearly defined endpoints and success criteria, planned statistical analyses, alternate strategies if primary approach fails, and realistic timelines. Power calculations and prior experience supporting feasibility should be shown. Potential technical issues and mitigation strategies should be discussed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary Data / Proof of Principle
rubrics_metrics.description: Preliminary in vivo data: one candidate peptide prevented diabetes onset in 90–96% of NOD mice (cohorts totaling ~200 mice) and reversed hyperglycemia in 57% of treated new-onset diabetic mice (24 mice tested, 12 reversals). Binding assays show peptide binds CD40 on T cells and remains stably bound in culture for 5 days. KGYY15 does not induce clotting in human blood in vitro.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strong preliminary efficacy, mechanistic binding assays, stability and safety (clotting) data increase reviewer confidence. Report sample sizes, p-values, and details of controls (scrambled peptide, RGD peptide, vehicle) to support claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure–Activity Relationship (Peptide design & stability)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rationale and SAR: peptides were designed around K-G-Y-Y motif from CD154; ExPaSY stability predictions and mass spectrometry used to assess stability. A glycine-scan identified critical positions (positions 2, 9, 11, 12 with Met12 critical). The 15-mer (KGYY15) was most stable and effective, 24-mer degraded rapidly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications must present mechanistic peptide design rationale, in vitro/in vivo SAR data, chemical stability analysis, and explain how SAR informs lead selection and formulation strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Endpoints and Outcome Measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary and secondary endpoints: diabetes diagnosis (blood glucose ≥250 mg/dl on 3 consecutive measures), euglycemia defined as <120 mg/dl, GTT criteria (reference to DPT-1 thresholds: fasting >126 mg/dl or sustained oral GTT >200 mg/dl), serum insulin and c-peptide, pancreatic islet histology scoring (0–4), immune cell subset analyses, cytokine production (IL-6, IFNγ, TNFα).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Endpoints must be clinically relevant, well-defined, and measurable. Use standard diagnostic thresholds and provide histologic scoring definitions. Plan serial measurements and correlate serum biomarkers with tissue-level findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Controls and Comparators
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of scrambled peptide and RGD peptide controls (non-CD40 binding region), vehicle controls, and diabetes-resistant BALB/c mice as negative controls; adoptive transfer experiments using NOD.scid recipients to demonstrate pathogenicity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appropriate negative and positive controls (scrambled, unrelated peptides, genetic/strain controls) are required to attribute effects specifically to the CD40-binding motif. Include concurrent control cohorts for each experiment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical Power and Sample Size Justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Sample size determination described: powered to 90% confidence requiring 10 mice per treatment group for main experiments; other calculations use t-test with alpha=0.05 and confidence 0.95; specific group counts (e.g. 5 test animals vs 2 controls for some GTTs to reach 95% confidence as determined by GraphPad Prism). Total animal counts given (e.g. 250 mice for treatment groups, 80 NOD.scid recipients).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications must include explicit power/sample size calculations, statistical tests planned, and justification of chosen N based on prior observed effect sizes. Discrepancies or underpowered groups should be addressed with contingency plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate Animal Welfare and Justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Animals: NOD, NOD.scid, BALB/c; justification of numbers; housing at accredited facility (PHS, AAALAC); IACUC-approved protocols; description of veterinary care, minimizing discomfort (limited injections, euthanasia at severe hyperglycemia, provision of insulin if maintained diabetic >1 week), use of analgesics when they do not alter results, euthanasia by CO2 followed by cervical dislocation per AVMA and IACUC guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals using vertebrate animals must justify species and numbers, describe housing and veterinary oversight, outline methods to minimize pain/distress, humane endpoints and euthanasia methods, and compliance with institutional and federal animal welfare standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safety, Toxicology and PK Plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledges known safety issue with anti-CD154 (platelet aggregation) and reports KGYY15 does not induce clotting in preliminary assays; Phase II will include PK and toxicology studies, extended pharmaco-kinetic studies, and immunogenicity assessments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan for safety testing (in vitro clotting, PK, toxicology) and immunogenicity must be explicit for IND support. Discuss precedent toxicities for comparator modalities and how proposed approach avoids them; include plans for GLP studies in later phases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mechanistic Rationale and Biomarker Strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Mechanistic premise: Th40 (CD4+CD40+) T cells are pathogenic in NOD mice and expanded in human T1D/pre-diabetic subjects; Th40 levels correlate with transplant failure and can identify T1D subjects (97% identified in a 268-subject cohort). The peptide binds CD40 and is hypothesized to modulate pathogenic T cell responses without broadly depleting immune cells.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers look for a clear mechanistic link between target modulation and disease biology, with biomarker strategy to measure target engagement (Th40 levels, cytokine profile) and translational justification from human data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Milestones, Timeline, and Project Management
rubrics_metrics.description: Time frame: Aim 1 requires 12 months; Goals 2 and 3 can be concurrent within 12 months; Phase II PK/tox studies up to 4 years. Milestones include lead candidate selection, demonstration of GTT impact, sustained insulin/c-peptide detection, and IND submission. Collaborators (Dr. John Carpenter for peptide development; CliniPace LLC for IND advancement) will be recruited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A credible milestone plan with realistic timelines, named expertise/collaborators, and clear go/no-go criteria is expected. Identify personnel and external consultants who will enable IND-enabling activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory, IP, and Translation Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Goal to submit IND to FDA after Phase II; patent coverage: PCT Application No. PCT/US2015/022033 with notification that patents will be awarded in US and Europe; engagement of consulting firm for IND filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications proposing a path to clinic should include IP status, regulatory pathway (IND), and plans for commercialization/translation including consulting or industry collaborators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource Sharing, Authentication, and Administrative Components
rubrics_metrics.description: Application components listed: Multiple PD/PI Leadership Plan; Consortium/Contractual Arrangements; Letters of Support; Resource Sharing Plan(s); Authentication of Key Biological and/or Chemical Resources; Appendix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete administrative sections (leadership plan, consortium agreements, letters of support, resource sharing, authentication of key reagents) are required and reviewers expect these to be present and appropriately detailed for reproducibility and compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select Agent Research Compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicit statement: 'No select agents will be used.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications must disclose select agent use or explicitly state none. Compliance with select agent regulations is required when applicable.
